clue.text: Beefeaters possibly replacing ravens with corgi after government cut

definitions.note: carnivores eat beef, among other meat; the plural noun matches

indicators.note: replacing here means placing the letters again in new positions, so the pool is rearranged
cut says a letter is chopped out of corgi

explanation.surface: The Tower of London swaps its famous ravens for a royal corgi after a budget cut, with the Yeoman Warders (Beefeaters) looking on.
explanation.walkthrough: Beefeaters are the Yeoman Warders at the Tower of London, where ravens are kept; a corgi is the royal dog. Take G out of CORGI to get CORI, then rearrange it with RAVENS.
explanation.definitionFit: Meat-eating animals literally eat beef, so the Tower guards' nickname becomes a playful description of flesh-eaters.

clue.text: Dognapper ultimately snatched Dalmatian for one?

definitions.text: Dognapper ultimately snatched Dalmatian for one?

indicators.note: snatched means the letter is taken away from the word, as a thief takes it

parts.note: a Dalmatian is a person from Dalmatia, part of Croatia, so is a Croat; 'for one' marks this as an example

indicators.note: ultimately points to the final letter of dognapper

parts.note: the last letter of dognapper is the one taken

explanation.surface: A dog thief finally grabs a spotty Dalmatian puppy, for reasons unknown.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: in The Hundred and One Dalmatians, the dognapper Cruella de Vil steals Dalmatians for their spotted fur. Remove R, the last letter of 'Dognapper', from CROAT.
explanation.definitionFit: Cruella de Vil wanted the puppies' fur to make a garment, so that garment is what the dognapper took them for.

clue.text: Stir up arguments in speech

indicators.note: in speech means the word is spoken, so we want the one that sounds like it

parts.note: rows (rhymes with cows) are noisy quarrels

explanation.surface: Debaters inflame their audience with the points they make in a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: To rouse a crowd is to stir it up, excite or provoke it to action.

clue.text: Things unfortunately getting heated up in Room 101

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the letters are read from the bottom, so backwards

parts.note: room in the sense of space, as in no room to move
CI is 101 in Roman numerals (C = 100, I = 1)

explanation.surface: Room 101, from Orwell's 1984 and the TV show, is where hated things are banished, here being heated.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Up' sits at the end but turns everything before it. 'Room 101' looks like one name, yet it splits into two pieces, and the definition spans the first four words.
explanation.definitionFit: Polar ice is melting as the planet warms, which is the unfortunate heating the definition describes.

clue.text: Not completely mature, but turning over a new leaf?

indicators.note: turning over says the shortened word is flipped to read backwards
not completely means the last letter is left off

parts.note: to mature is to grow
N is an abbreviation for new, as in NT for New Testament

explanation.surface: Someone half-grown claims to be turning over a new leaf, reforming their ways.
explanation.walkthrough: GRO, reversed by 'turning over', gives ORG; A and N follow. 'Turning over a new leaf' reads as one idiom, but only 'leaf' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically a leaf is one of a plant's organs, a structure with a particular function, so this is a definition by example.

clue.text: Endless send-up on organised religion shows persistence

indicators.note: in a down clue, A on B puts A above, so before, B
endless means the word loses both its end letters

parts.note: to organise something is to run it, past tense ran
CE is the Church of England, standing for religion

explanation.surface: A satire mocking organised religion shows great staying power.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance is the ability to keep going through hardship, the same staying power as persistence.

clue.text: Where film will end up, one way or another

definitions.text: Where film will end up, one way or another

parts.words: Where film will end up, one way or another
parts.note: a camera film ends up being developed somewhere kept free of light, and a cinema film is watched with the lights off

explanation.walkthrough: Both senses of film work: camera film is developed in a light-free room, and a movie is watched with the lights off.
explanation.definitionFit: A photographer's developing room is kept without light so that film is not spoiled.

clue.text: He's bald, no? Perhaps — but she's this

indicators.note: perhaps suggests the letters could be put another way, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A man asks if he is bald; perhaps, but his partner has pale fair hair to spare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He's' and 'she's' set up a couple; the definition is just 'she's this', a description of a woman.
explanation.definitionFit: Ash blonde is a pale, greyish shade of fair hair, so a woman with it is described this way.

clue.text: King with valuable resource acting neutral about fresh conflict

parts.note: K is the chess abbreviation for king
ore is mined rock containing metal
A is the abbreviation for acting, as in a military rank (A/Capt)
N is the abbreviation for neutral, as on a gear lever or electrical plug

indicators.note: about says the word is turned round to read backwards

parts.note: fresh as in raw, uncooked

explanation.surface: A monarch with a precious resource stays neutral while a new war breaks out.
explanation.definitionFit: The Korean War (1950-53) was an armed conflict between North and South Korea and their allies.

clue.text: Crews on either side of English river

indicators.note: on either side of means the first word goes around the letter, enclosing it

parts.note: gangs are crews of workers

explanation.surface: Rowing crews line both banks of an English river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Ganges is the great sacred river of northern India, flowing into the Bay of Bengal.

clue.text: Jazz quartet occasionally ripped off Kind of Blue

indicators.note: occasionally ripped off means every other letter is torn away, leaving alternate ones

explanation.surface: A jazz quartet is accused of plagiarising Miles Davis's album Kind of Blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Kind of Blue is the famous Miles Davis jazz album, but here the definition simply means a type of blue.
explanation.definitionFit: Azure is a bright sky blue, one shade or type within the blue family.

clue.text: Top gangster got that woman to collect notes from minor triad

indicators.note: to collect means the first pieces gather the notes up inside them

parts.note: taken as written
the D minor triad, a three-note chord, is D, F, A
her refers to a woman

explanation.surface: A mob boss has his girl pick up cash from a junior gang branch.
explanation.walkthrough: In the surface, notes are banknotes and the triad is a Chinese gang; in the wordplay they are the musical notes of the D minor chord.
explanation.definitionFit: A godfather is the head of a Mafia family, as in the Puzo novel and Coppola film.

clue.text: Gripped by Beatlemania, geriatric recalled Get Back

indicators.note: recalled, as in called back, says the letters run backwards
gripped by says the letters are held within the words that follow

explanation.surface: An elderly Beatles fanatic remembers the song Get Back.
explanation.walkthrough: Get Back is a Beatles song, which makes it look like a title; it is just the phrasal verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To regain something is to recover it after losing it.

clue.text: Royal property unequally divided between Regan and Cordelia

indicators.note: unequally divided between says the two names are each cut and shared out, four letters from one and three from the other

explanation.surface: King Lear's kingdom is split unfairly between his daughters Regan and Cordelia.
explanation.walkthrough: Regan and Cordelia are King Lear's daughters, apt for royal property. Keep REGA from the first and LIA from the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Regalia are the emblems of royalty, such as crown, sceptre and orb.

clue.text: Crew member gets more than one flyer to put away a bit of technology

indicators.note: put away in the sense of eating, so each flyer swallows a binary digit
to here means pressed up to and into, setting one digit inside the first flyer

parts.note: two flyers side by side: a bat and a swan
a bit is a binary digit, which can be shown as a zero, the letter O
the other binary digit of computing, one, shown as the letter I

explanation.surface: A sailor receives several leaflets about storing a gadget.
explanation.walkthrough: A bit is a binary digit, 0 or 1, shown here as O and I. BAT eats O to give BOAT, and SWAN eats I to give SWAIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A boatswain, or bosun, is the ship's officer in charge of deck crew and equipment.

clue.text: Pricklier British fiction hidden within covers of bestseller by American

indicators.note: by means next to, so the pieces sit side by side
hidden within says the word goes inside the outer letters
covers of means the outside letters, first and last

parts.note: a lie is a fiction, an untruth

explanation.surface: A spiky British novel is tucked inside the jacket of an American bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: Brambles are thorny shrubs, so the more bramble-covered a thing is, the more prickly.

clue.text: I miss a lot when drunk or very high

indicators.note: drunk suggests letters staggering into a new order

explanation.surface: A tipsy person admits missing a lot of what goes on once they're very high.
explanation.definitionFit: Altissimo is a musical term for the highest register of a voice or instrument.

clue.text: Swimmer's called inconsiderate when putting beginners off

definitions.note: the clue's 's is is, so the definition is the noun swimmer

indicators.note: beginners are first letters, which are put off, removed from each word

parts.note: rang as in phoned, called up
selfish people are inconsiderate of others

explanation.surface: A swimmer is branded thoughtless when making novices give up.
explanation.definitionFit: An angelfish is a brightly coloured tropical fish, so is a swimmer.

clue.text: One joins transgressive act that's a bit disgusting

definitions.note: the definition reads as a noun phrase, a thing that joins

parts.note: a sin is a transgression
ew is a mild cry of disgust, something you say at a thing that is a bit disgusting

explanation.surface: Someone joins in a wicked deed that is rather revolting.
explanation.definitionFit: A sinew is a tendon, the tough cord that connects a muscle to bone.

clue.text: To begin with, analyst claimed that erotic dynamic was in play?

indicators.note: to begin with points to the first letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A therapist claims a sexual dynamic was at work in a relationship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Was in play' looks like 'was at work'; read it as 'performed in a play'.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who acted performed a role on stage in a play.

clue.text: Potentially hammer frames for delicate, fragile art

indicators.note: frames means the outer letters, the frame around each word

explanation.surface: A hammer could destroy frames holding delicate, fragile artworks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Potentially' is there because beating someone needn't mean hammering them; defeat can be narrow.
explanation.definitionFit: To hammer an opponent is to beat them heavily, a decisive win over them.

clue.text: Stars from BGT are repeatedly manipulated

indicators.note: repeatedly manipulated: the little word is taken over and over, then all the letters are worked into a new order

parts.note: BGT is Britain's Got Talent, the TV talent show

explanation.surface: Contestants on Britain's Got Talent are repeatedly manipulated by producers.
explanation.walkthrough: BGT is Britain's Got Talent, a TV talent show whose acts are called stars, which sets up the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The Great Bear, Ursa Major, is a constellation, a group of stars.

clue.text: Startled criminal drops back on all fours

indicators.note: criminal suggests something bent or crooked, so the letters are rearranged
drops means a letter falls out of the word
the back of all is its last letter

explanation.surface: A shocked crook collapses onto hands and knees.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On all fours' reads as one phrase, but 'back on all' gives L, leaving only 'fours' as the definition. Without L, STARTLED leaves STARTED, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group or set of four, so tetrads are fours.

clue.text: Fellow with a blush in animation

definitions.text: Fellow with a blush in animation

indicators.note: animation means lively movement, so the letters are stirred into a new order

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fellow, as in FRS

explanation.surface: A cartoon character blushes with a fellow beside him.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also defines: in Disney's animated Snow White, Bashful is the dwarf who blushes.
explanation.definitionFit: Bashful is the shy, easily embarrassed dwarf in Disney's Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs.

clue.text: Fetched bad actor on location for Batman

parts.note: got as in went and fetched
a ham is an overacting performer

explanation.surface: A film crew fetched a poor actor on set for a Batman shoot.
explanation.definitionFit: Gotham City is the fictional city where the comic-book hero Batman fights crime.

clue.text: Green vegan jam sandwiches

indicators.note: sandwiches as a verb means holds between, so the answer is inside these words

explanation.surface: Eco-friendly vegan jam sandwiches.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' looks like an adjective for the food; it is slang for cannabis.
explanation.definitionFit: Green is slang for marijuana, and ganja is another name for the same drug.

clue.text: Single person who'll never settle down caught bouquet

indicators.note: caught as in caught by the ear, heard, so we want a sound-alike

parts.words: Single person who'll never settle down
parts.note: a means one, single; a roamer is a wanderer who never settles

explanation.surface: A footloose bachelor catches the bouquet at a wedding.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech, 'a roamer' sounds like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A wine's bouquet is its characteristic smell, its scent.

clue.text: Booze store making Methuselah's head spin

indicators.note: spin means the letter is turned upside down, which here gives a different letter

parts.note: a mine is a store or rich supply

indicators.note: head means the first letter of Methuselah

explanation.surface: The setter, Methuselah, finds the booze cupboard makes his head spin.
explanation.walkthrough: Methuselah is the setter's pseudonym and also a large wine bottle. Turning the M at the top of MINE upside down gives W.
explanation.definitionFit: Wine is an alcoholic drink, so it counts as booze.

clue.text: Sham leader is out of control

indicators.note: leader is out of says the first letter is removed

parts.note: a limitation is a control or restriction

explanation.surface: A sham leader is out of control.
explanation.definitionFit: A sham is a fake, a copy passing itself off as the real thing.

clue.text: Regular features in tabloid describing more of the same from Simon Mayo

indicators.note: describing in the sense of drawing a line around, so the first letters enclose the others
regular features are every other letter of the word
more of the same means taking alternate letters again, this time of the name

explanation.surface: A tabloid writes about radio host Simon Mayo giving more of the same.
explanation.walkthrough: Simon Mayo is a British radio presenter; 'Mayo' alone is short for mayonnaise.
explanation.definitionFit: Aioli is a garlic mayonnaise from Provence, so it is a kind of mayo.

clue.text: See 6
Mean person putting move on ice after budget

indicators.note: after places the move second, following the other piece

parts.note: budget as an adjective means cheap, as in budget airline
to skate is to move on ice

explanation.surface: A skater makes a move on the rink after a cheap warm-up.
explanation.definitionFit: A cheapskate is a stingy person who hates spending money.
